name: Salesforce Commerce Cloud
description: Ecommerce: Salesforce's enterprise B2C Commerce platform with SCAPI/OCAPI REST APIs for storefronts (Shopper APIs) and merchant operations (Admin APIs).
access_notes: SCAPI is included at no extra cost for B2C Commerce customers, but you must be a customer (or registered partner) with an Account Manager org to create API clients, SLAS clients, and sandboxes. Shopper APIs use SLAS (OAuth 2.1: authorization_code_pkce, client_credentials); Admin APIs use Account Manager client_credentials only. Tokens are JWTs sent as Bearer. No public self-serve signup for credentials.
mcp_notes: Official B2C DX MCP Server (@salesforce/b2c-dx-mcp, SalesforceCommerceCloud GitHub org) is a developer-tooling MCP covering SCAPI, cartridge deploys, and Managed Runtime; it still requires B2C Commerce instance credentials. No Composio toolkit found for Salesforce Commerce Cloud (Composio's 'salesforce' toolkit targets the CRM).
uncertainty_notes: Could not confirm a native outbound webhook/event-push feature for B2C Commerce in official SCAPI docs (extensibility is via hooks/custom APIs/jobs); left supports_webhooks null. On-demand sandboxes require an existing customer/partner realm.

evidence.note: OAuth 2.1-based scopes; both Admin and Shopper APIs use JWT access tokens with Bearer scheme; Admin via Account Manager, Shopper via SLAS.
Admin APIs: create API client in Account Manager; 'only the client_credentials grant type is supported'.
SLAS grant-type table: authorization_code_pkce, authorization_code, client_credentials for shopper tokens.
'For B2C Commerce customers, the API is available at no extra cost' — access presumes an existing B2C Commerce instance/sandbox; Admin APIs are read+write across products, orders, inventory.
Official docs for the B2C DX MCP Server (@salesforce/b2c-dx-mcp) connecting AI assistants to B2C Commerce environments.
